models_evaluated: Med-Diet (DeepSeek-R1 with integrated clinical dietary guidelines)

links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of dietary plans, guideline-grounded Med-Diet versus general-purpose LLMs
links.effect: Med-Diet mean score 4.09 ± 0.64 versus DeepSeek-R1 3.60 ± 0.68, GPT-4o 3.33, GLM-Z1-32B 3.35, Llama-3.3-70B 3.00; higher on accuracy and safety (all p < 0.05).
links.quote: Med-Diet received higher mean preference scores from expert evaluators compared to all baseline LLMs (mean score of 4.09 ± 0.64).

links.outcome: Nutritionist efficiency and expert-rated plan quality without versus with Med-Diet assistance
links.effect: Median time fell from 17.5 to 13.0 min (p < 0.05); accuracy, personalization, practicality and overall scores were higher in the Med-Diet-assisted group (adjusted p < 0.05). Overreliance was not assessed.
links.quote: Expert scores for accuracy, personalization, practicality, and overall recommendation were higher in the Med-Diet-assisted group (adjusted p < 0.05).

screen.reason: The study describes the development and simulated evaluation of an LLM agent (Med-Diet) for generating chronic disease dietary plans, including reader-study evaluation and clinician-in-the-loop performance comparison with vs. without the tool, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
